official.description_text:
Doctoral student in Nuclear Power Safety
Apply for position
School of Engineering Sciences at KTH
Project description
Third-cycle subject:
Physics, specialization in Nuclear Engineering
The group of Nuclear Power Safety in Division of Nuclear Science and Engineering (NSE) conducts research on accident phenomena of risk importance to existing and future nuclear reactors, and performs safety analysis for nuclear power plants, including design basis accident analysis and severe accident analysis. The research projects involve extensive international cooperation.
We are looking for a doctoral student to carry out frontier research on accident management (AM) during severe accidents of light water reactors. The doctoral student project is supported by the funds from Strålsäkerhetsmyndigheten (SSM).
The successful candidate is expected to (i) digitalize the paper-based, lookup-table-like procedures in the severe accident management guidelines (SAMG) to be chosen, facilitating the realization of the SAMG in case of severe accidents; (ii) develop an AI-aided tool for diagnosis of plant damage state using measured and estimated data (e.g. the simulation results of U.S. NRC codes); and (iii) combine the digitalized SAMG with the AI-aided tool for effective accident management.
Supervision:
Professor Weimin Ma is proposed to supervise the doctoral student. Decisions are made on admission
Admission requirements
To be admitted to postgraduate education (Chapter 7, 39 § Swedish Higher Education Ordinance), the applicant must have basic eligibility in accordance with either of the following:
passed a second cycle degree (for example a master's degree), or
completed course requirements of at least 240 higher education credits, of which at least 60 second-cycle higher education credits, or
acquired, in some other way within or outside the country, substantially equivalent knowledge
The applicant must have been awarded a Master’s degree in nuclear engineering or mechanical engineering.
In addition to the above, there is also a
mandatory requirement for English equivalent to English B/6.
Selection
In order to succeed as a doctoral student at KTH you need to be goal oriented and persevering in your work. During the selection process, candidates will be assessed upon their ability to:
independently pursue his or her work
collaborate with others,
have a professional approach and
analyze and work with complex issues.
After the qualification requirements, great emphasis will be placed on personal skills.
Target degree: Doctoral degree
Information regarding admission and employment
Only those admitted to postgraduate education may be employed as a doctoral student. The total length of employment may not be longer than what corresponds to full-time doctoral education in four years' time. An employed doctoral student can, to a limited extent (maximum 20%), perform certain tasks within their role, e.g. training and administration. A new position as a doctoral student is for a maximum of one year, and then the employment may be renewed for a maximum of two years at a time. In the case of studies that are to be completed with a licentiate degree, the total period of employment may not be longer than what corresponds to full-time doctoral education for two years.
As a doctoral student, you are entitled to a workplace with
many employee benefits
and monthly salary according to

ai.summary: KTH Royal Institute of Technology seeks a doctoral student in Nuclear Power Safety to digitalize severe-accident-management guidelines (SAMG), develop AI-aided plant-damage diagnosis tools, and integrate these for improved accident management in light-water reactors. The research combines accident phenomenology, nuclear engineering, AI/machine learning for diagnosis, and safety analysis procedures.

thematic_fit.rationale: Position is rooted in nuclear engineering, accident analysis, and reactor safety—pure technical physics and engineering domains. The researcher's expertise is in human-centred XR, immersive learning, spatial cognition, and collaborative systems. There is no thematic intersection. The mention of 'AI-aided diagnosis' does not represent human-centred HCI; it is a machine-learning engineering task applied to reactor telemetry data. The core is nuclear safety, not human factors or interaction design.

methodological_fit.rationale: Position requires a Master's degree in nuclear engineering or mechanical engineering and demands deep physics and engineering knowledge. The researcher has intermediate experimental-design and quantitative-research skills from HCI user studies—not aligned with nuclear accident simulation, code-based phenomenology analysis, or diagnostic ML model development. No methodological bridge.

growth_value.rationale: This role would require learning nuclear engineering and accident phenomenology from the ground up. It does not close any of the researcher's stated capability gaps (statistics, mixed-effects modelling, physiological sensing, eye-tracking) in a useful way. Growth would be in a completely orthogonal domain.

strategic_value.rationale: Strengths: KTH (Stockholm, Sweden) is in a priority-1 geography (Scandinavia). This IS a doctoral-student position aligned with target position types. Supervision by Prof. Weimin Ma; strong institution. Weaknesses: Research community is nuclear engineering and safety science, not HCI or immersive systems. Publications and conferences are in nuclear technology, not XR/immersive-systems venues. Doctoral training embeds researcher in nuclear-engineering networks, not target research community. Post-PhD trajectory would be nuclear-safety research, not human-centred immersive systems.

eligibility_flags: Admission requirement: 'Master's degree in nuclear engineering or mechanical engineering.' Researcher holds MSc by Research in Creative Multimedia (Faculty of Creative Multimedia). Field mismatch is substantial. Eligibility depends on whether the program accepts 'substantially equivalent knowledge,' which is unlikely given the disciplinary distance.
Admission requires English proficiency 'equivalent to English B/6.' Researcher's background does not specify, but is likely satisfied given prior international research context.

Position may require security clearance under Swedish Protective Security Act (2018:585) due to nuclear-safety sensitivity. Researcher's background as a foreign graduate student may trigger additional vetting; posting notes 'a prerequisite for employment is that the applicant is approved following the security clearance.'
risks: Researcher does not hold a Master's degree in nuclear engineering or mechanical engineering. Eligibility for PhD admission is questionable; program is unlikely to accept Creative Multimedia as 'substantially equivalent.'
Zero background in nuclear physics, reactor systems, or safety analysis. Doctoral training would require 1–2 years of foundational coursework before independent research.

Position focuses on accident management procedures and AI diagnosis tools—technical engineering domains. The research has no human-computer-interaction or human-factors component despite the mention of 'digitalize...procedures.'
Security clearance for nuclear-sensitive work may be complex for a foreign researcher; processing delays or denial is possible.
Post-PhD career path would be nuclear engineering, not immersive systems or HCI research.
